title: Hugs, cuddles, or kisses offered to a person
summary: Most children show affection, for example with a hug, a cuddle, or a kiss, by about 15 months, CDC says.
body: The gestures on this line are aimed at the caregiver. Hugging a stuffed toy is a different line on the same page. CDC does not rank hug above kiss. Its bar is most children, written as 75 percent or more, and a child who shows fondness in some other way is not failed by this card. The list is American, and it is not a screening instrument.

sources.title: Milestones by 15 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US government public domain. Supports 'Shows you affection (hugs, cuddles, or kisses you)'.
